projects.title: Hello, World!
projects.description: Your first C++ program. Learn the basics of compiling, running and printing to the console.
projects.output: Hello, C++!
projects.explanation: Every C++ program starts execution at main(). The <iostream> header brings in cout, the standard output stream, and endl flushes the stream and moves to a new line.

projects.title: Simple Calculator
projects.description: Perform basic arithmetic operations (add, subtract, multiply, divide) with user input.
projects.output:
Enter first number: 12
Enter operator (+, -, *, /): *
Enter second number: 4
Result: 48
projects.explanation: A switch statement selects the operation based on the operator character. Division by zero is guarded explicitly to avoid undefined behaviour.

projects.title: Even or Odd Checker
projects.description: Check whether a number is even or odd using conditions.
projects.output:
Enter an integer: 17
17 is Odd.
projects.explanation: The modulus operator % gives the remainder of division by 2. A remainder of 0 means the number is even.

projects.title: Largest of Three Numbers
projects.description: Find the largest number among three numbers entered by the user.
projects.output:
Enter three numbers: 4 19 7
Largest number: 19
projects.explanation: We start by assuming the first value is the largest, then compare it against the other two, updating whenever a bigger value is found.

projects.title: Leap Year Checker
projects.description: Determine whether a given year is a leap year.
projects.output:
Enter a year: 2028
2028 is a Leap Year.
projects.explanation: A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4 but not by 100, unless it is also divisible by 400 (e.g. 2000).

projects.title: Multiplication Table
projects.description: Print the multiplication table of a number using a loop.
projects.output:
Enter a number: 7
7 x 1 = 7
7 x 2 = 14
...
7 x 10 = 70
projects.explanation: A for loop counts from 1 to 10, multiplying the chosen number by the counter each iteration.

projects.title: Factorial Calculator
projects.description: Calculate the factorial of a number using a loop or recursion.
projects.output:
Enter a non-negative integer: 6
6! = 720
projects.explanation: The factorial function multiplies every integer from 2 up to n. unsigned long long is used so larger factorials do not overflow as quickly.

projects.title: Fibonacci Series
projects.description: Print the Fibonacci series up to n terms.
projects.output:
Enter number of terms: 8
Fibonacci Series: 0 1 1 2 3 5 8 13
projects.explanation: Each Fibonacci number is the sum of the two numbers before it. Two variables track the previous two terms as the loop advances.

projects.title: Prime Number Checker
projects.description: Check whether a given number is prime.
projects.output:
Enter a number: 29
29 is a Prime Number.
projects.explanation: A number is prime if no integer from 2 up to its square root divides it evenly. Checking only up to sqrt(n) keeps the loop efficient.

projects.title: Prime Numbers in a Range
projects.description: Print all prime numbers within a given range.
projects.output:
Enter range (low high): 10 30
Prime numbers: 11 13 17 19 23 29
projects.explanation: The isPrime helper from the previous project is reused inside a loop that scans every number in the requested range.

projects.title: Palindrome Number
projects.description: Check whether a number reads the same forwards and backwards.
projects.output:
Enter a number: 12321
12321 is a Palindrome.
projects.explanation: The digits of the number are peeled off one at a time with % 10 and rebuilt in reverse order, then compared to the original.

projects.title: Armstrong Number
projects.description: Check whether a number is an Armstrong number (sum of its own digits, each raised to the power of the digit count, equals the number).
projects.output:
Enter a number: 153
153 is an Armstrong number.
projects.explanation: First the digit count is found, then each digit is raised to that power and summed. If the sum equals the original number, it is an Armstrong number.

projects.title: Reverse a Number
projects.description: Reverse the digits of an integer.
projects.output:
Enter a number: 48293
Reversed number: 39284
projects.explanation: This is the same digit-extraction technique used in the palindrome checker, applied here purely to build and display the reversed value.

projects.title: Sum of Digits
projects.description: Calculate the sum of the digits of a number.
projects.output:
Enter a number: 4829
Sum of digits: 23
projects.explanation: Each digit is extracted with % 10 and added to a running total, while / 10 removes that digit before the next iteration.

projects.title: Number Guessing Game
projects.description: Guess a randomly generated number within a limited number of attempts.
projects.output:
Guess the number between 1 and 100!
Attempt 1/7: 50
Too low!
Attempt 2/7: 75
Correct! You guessed it in 2 attempts.
projects.explanation: rand() % 100 + 1 generates a pseudo-random target. A do-while loop keeps prompting until the guess matches or attempts run out.

projects.title: Rock Paper Scissors
projects.description: Play Rock, Paper, Scissors against the computer.
projects.output:
0-Rock  1-Paper  2-Scissors
Enter your choice: 0
Computer chose: Scissors
You win!
projects.explanation: Choices are encoded as 0, 1, 2. The three winning combinations for the user are checked explicitly against the computer's random pick.

projects.title: Simple Quiz Game
projects.description: A short multiple-question quiz that scores the player at the end.
projects.output:
What is the capital of France? Paris
Correct!
5 + 7 = ? 12
Correct!
Which language is this program written in? Python
Wrong! Correct answer: c++
You scored 2 out of 3.
projects.explanation: Answers are normalised to lowercase before comparison so the check is not case sensitive, and a running score tracks correct responses.

projects.title: Student Grade Calculator
projects.description: Calculate a student's average marks and assign a letter grade.
projects.output:
Enter marks for subject 1: 88
... 
Average: 79.4
Grade: B
projects.explanation: Marks for each subject are stored in an array, summed, and averaged. The average is then mapped to a letter grade using a chain of conditions.

projects.title: Student Management System
projects.description: Add, view and search student records using a struct and a vector.
projects.output:
1. Add Student  2. View Students  3. Exit
Choice: 1
Roll number: 12
Name: Riya
Marks: 91
Student added successfully!
projects.explanation: A struct groups related fields for one student, and a vector holds a dynamic list of them. Functions keep the menu logic and data handling separate.

projects.title: Bank Account Management
projects.description: Simulate deposit, withdrawal and balance inquiry using a class.
projects.output:
1. Deposit 2. Withdraw 3. Balance 4. Exit
Choice: 3
Arjun's balance: 5000
projects.explanation: The class encapsulates the owner and balance as private data, exposing only deposit, withdraw and showBalance as the public interface.

projects.title: Contact Management System
projects.description: Store contacts and search for one by name.
projects.output:
1. Add 2. Search 3. List All 4. Exit
Choice: 2
Search name: Meera
Meera -> 9876543210
projects.explanation: Contacts are stored as structs inside a vector. std::find_if scans the vector with a lambda predicate to locate a contact by name.

projects.title: Library Management System
projects.description: Issue and return books while tracking availability.
projects.output:
Library Books:
1. C++ Primer [Available]
2. Data Structures [Available]
3. Algorithms [Available]
1. Issue 2. Return 3. Exit
Choice: 1
Book number: 1
Book issued.
projects.explanation: Each Book object tracks its own issued flag. The menu loop lets the user toggle that flag for a chosen book by index.

projects.title: ATM Simulation
projects.description: Simulate a PIN-protected ATM with deposit, withdrawal and balance checks.
projects.output:
Enter PIN: 1234
1. Balance 2. Deposit 3. Withdraw 4. Exit
Choice: 1
Balance: 10000
projects.explanation: The ATM class hides the PIN and balance as private members. authenticate() checks the PIN before menu() is allowed to run.

projects.title: Employee Management System
projects.description: Manage employee records including salary calculations.
projects.output:
Number of employees: 1
Name: Sanjana
Basic salary: 40000
Sanjana -> Net Salary: 44000.00
projects.explanation: Net salary adds a 20% house rent allowance and deducts a 10% tax from the basic salary, demonstrating simple business-rule calculations.

projects.title: Expense Tracker
projects.description: Track daily expenses and view a category-wise total.
projects.output:
1. Add Expense 2. View Summary 3. Exit
Choice: 2
Food: 1200
Travel: 500
Total spent: 1700
projects.explanation: A std::map groups expenses by category automatically, since map keys are kept sorted and each new amount is added to that category's running total.

projects.title: To-Do List
projects.description: Add, complete and remove tasks from a simple to-do list.
projects.output:
--- To-Do List ---
1. [ ] Finish DS assignment

1. Add 2. Mark Done 3. Remove 4. Exit
Choice: 2
Task number: 1
projects.explanation: Each Task struct stores its text and a done flag. vector::erase removes a task by its position when the user chooses to delete it.

projects.title: Digital Clock
projects.description: Display the current system time, updating every second.
projects.output:
Digital Clock (Ctrl+C to stop)
2026-9-11  14:22:35
projects.explanation: time() and localtime() read the system clock into a tm struct. The loop reprints the time every second using \r to overwrite the same line.

projects.title: Unit Converter
projects.description: Convert between common units such as kilometers/miles and kilograms/pounds.
projects.output:
1. KM to Miles
2. Miles to KM
3. KG to Pounds
4. Pounds to KG
Choice: 1
Enter value: 10
6.21371 miles
projects.explanation: Each conversion is a fixed multiplication or division factor selected through a switch statement based on the user's menu choice.

projects.title: Temperature Converter
projects.description: Convert temperatures between Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin.
projects.output:
Enter temperature in Celsius: 25
25 C = 77 F
25 C = 298.15 K
projects.explanation: Fahrenheit and Kelvin are both computed directly from the standard conversion formulas relative to Celsius.

projects.title: Currency Converter
projects.description: Convert an amount from one currency to another using fixed exchange rates.
projects.output:
From currency (USD/INR/EUR/GBP): INR
To currency (USD/INR/EUR/GBP): USD
Amount: 1000
1000 INR = 12 USD
projects.explanation: Every currency is first converted to a common base (USD), then from USD to the target currency, avoiding the need for a rate between every possible pair.

projects.title: Tic Tac Toe
projects.description: A two-player Tic Tac Toe game played on the console.
projects.explanation: The board is a 2D char array. checkWin scans every row, column and both diagonals for three matching symbols after each move.

projects.title: Hangman Game
projects.description: Guess the hidden word letter by letter before running out of attempts.
projects.output:
Word: ___________   Attempts left: 6
Guess a letter: p
Word: p__________   Attempts left: 6
projects.explanation: A std::set stores guessed letters without duplicates. The hidden word is redrawn each round, revealing any letter that has already been guessed correctly.

projects.title: Inventory Management System
projects.description: Track stock items, quantities and restock alerts.
projects.output:
1. Add Item 2. Sell Item 3. View Inventory 4. Exit
Choice: 3
Keyboard | Qty: 3 | Price: 799  [LOW STOCK]
projects.explanation: Selling an item reduces its quantity after checking enough stock exists. The inventory view flags any item under 5 units as low stock.

projects.title: File Handling Notes Manager
projects.description: Save and read text notes from a file using fstream.
projects.output:
1. Add Note 2. View Notes
Choice: 1
Enter note: Submit DS assignment by Friday
Note saved!
projects.explanation: ofstream with ios::app appends new notes to notes.txt without erasing existing ones. ifstream reads it back line by line with getline.

projects.title: Mini Banking System
projects.description: A multi-account banking system supporting account creation, deposits, withdrawals and transfers.
projects.output:
1. Open Account 2. Deposit 3. Withdraw 4. Transfer 5. View All 6. Exit
Choice: 1
Owner name: Kabir
Initial deposit: 2000
Account created with ID 1001
projects.explanation: Accounts live in a vector and are looked up by ID with a pointer-returning helper, which lets deposit, withdraw and transfer all share the same lookup logic.
